Free Offer of the Gospel
free AW-fer uhv thuh GOS-puhl
doctrinal phrase
From free offer (a sincere proffer made without price or partiality) and gospel; the well-meant offer of Christ to all who hear.

See also: Free Offer of the Gospel

📖 Biblical Definition

The free offer of the gospel, also called the well-meant or sincere offer, is the doctrine that in the preaching of the gospel God genuinely and freely offers Christ and salvation to all who hear, commanding all to repent and believe, and promising life to everyone who comes. This offer is universal in its proclamation and sincere in its terms: the call goes out indiscriminately to sinners of every kind, the invitations are real, and God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked but calls him to turn and live. The Reformed faith holds the free offer together with the sovereign decree of election, without collapsing either into the other. God has from eternity chosen a definite people, and Christ’s atonement effectually secures their salvation; yet the gospel is preached to all, the offer is sincere to all, and the responsibility of every hearer to believe is real, so that those who refuse perish justly by their own unbelief. The two truths are not contradictory but are held in their proper places: God’s secret decree belongs to Him, and the revealed call and offer belong to us, and our duty is to preach Christ freely to all and to bid every sinner come. The dictionary holds the free offer against two errors—the hyper-Calvinism that denies any offer to the non-elect and so chills evangelism, and the Arminianism that grounds the offer in a universal atonement and a sovereign-less grace. The gospel is to be freely offered to all, sincerely and without reserve, and whosoever will may come and take the water of life freely.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The doctrine that in preaching, God sincerely offers Christ and salvation to all who hear, commanding all to believe—held together with sovereign election, against both hyper-Calvinism and Arminianism.

FREE OFFER OF THE GOSPEL, the sincere offer of Christ to all who hear.

Universal in proclamation, sincere in its terms, commanding all to repent and believe.

God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but calls him to turn and live.

Held together with sovereign election and definite atonement, without contradiction.

Against hyper-Calvinism, which denies the offer, and Arminianism, which grounds it in universal atonement.

📖 Key Scripture

Isa 55:1 — "Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price."

Eze 33:11 — "Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?"

Mat 11:28 — "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."

Rev 22:17 — "And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The free offer is denied by hyper-Calvinism and distorted by Arminianism, which grounds it in a universal, ineffectual atonement.

expand to see more

The corruption on one side is hyper-Calvinism, which, zealous for the decree of election, denies that God offers Christ to the non-elect at all, and so refuses to bid all sinners come. This chills evangelism and contradicts the plain Scripture in which God invites every one that thirsts, commands all men everywhere to repent, and declares that He has no pleasure in the death of the wicked but calls him to turn and live. The free, sincere offer to all who hear is the warrant of all gospel preaching.

The corruption on the other side is Arminianism, which secures the universality of the offer by denying the particularity of the atonement and the sovereignty of grace—teaching that Christ died alike for all and that the offer’s sincerity requires a salvation God equally intends for every man. The dictionary holds both truths in their places: God genuinely and freely offers Christ to all who hear, and the responsibility of every hearer is real; yet election is sovereign and the atonement effectual for the elect. The secret decree belongs to God; the revealed offer belongs to us. Our duty is to preach Christ freely to all, and the door stands open: whosoever will may come and take the water of life freely.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The phrase names the sincere universal offer of Christ, held in harmony with sovereign election and definite atonement.

expand to see more

“Free” — offered without price, without partiality, without reserve.

“Offer” — a sincere proffer of Christ to all who hear the gospel.

Also “the well-meant offer” or “the sincere offer.”

Grounded in God’s revealed will and command, not His secret decree.

Held against hyper-Calvinism on one hand and Arminianism on the other.

Usage

"The free offer of the gospel is the warrant for bidding all sinners come to Christ."

"It is held together with election and definite atonement, against hyper-Calvinism."

"Its sincerity is grounded in God’s revealed will, not a universal atonement."
